mainTopic: Sending הלכות in writing, offering נסכים at night, and the offerings brought during the festival
overview: The amud opens by finishing a ruling about מנחת נסכים. Nothing needs to be erased from the ברייתא, because one ברייתא speaks of נסכים brought with a זבח and the other of נסכים brought by themselves. The גמרא then asks how such a ruling could be sent in a letter at all, since רבי יוחנן and a פסוק teach that writing down הלכות is forbidden. The answer is that a new teaching may be different, based on 'עת לעשות לה׳': it is better to set aside one rule than to let the תורה be forgotten. Back on נסכים, רב פפא rules that נסכים brought by themselves may be made holy and offered at night, a ברייתא supports him, and רב אדא בר אהבה adds that dawn disqualifies them. Next comes רבי יוחנן's word-by-word reading of the פסוק about festival offerings, which adds required offerings of individuals, compares נסכים to שלמים, and includes שלמי נזיר. אביי objects that a נזיר's offering is voluntary, and the reply is to remove ״נזירות״ from his source. The גמרא challenges this from אבשלום, who went to pay his vow in חברון. It concludes that he really went there to sacrifice, since private altars were permitted, and then asks from when the 'forty years' in that פסוק are counted.

steps.title: Keep the words in the ברייתא and split the cases instead
steps.stepSummary: The message says not to erase 'מנחת נסכים' from the ברייתא. The two ברייתות do not really clash. One speaks about נסכים brought with a זבח, and the other speaks about נסכים brought by themselves.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do not erase the words 'the meal offering of libations' from the ברייתא. There is no contradiction. One ברייתא is about libations that come with an animal offering. The other is about libations that come on their own.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the ruling that was supposed to be sent: keep the text of the ברייתא as it is, and solve the contradiction by splitting the cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the way to settle the clash between the two ברייתות was to erase 'מנחת נסכים' from one of them. Now a gentler fix is offered. When נסכים come with a זבח, their מנחה is offered only by day. When נסכים come by themselves, their מנחה may be offered at night. Both texts stay as they are, because each one describes a different situation.

keyTerms.meaning: Erase or delete (words from a text)
The flour offering that goes along with libations
It is not difficult; there is no real contradiction
Brought together with an animal offering
Brought on their own, without an animal offering

steps.whatToRemember: The מנחה of נסכים that come with a זבח is offered only by day. The מנחה of נסכים brought by themselves may be offered at night.

phrases.english: And he should not delete 'the meal offering of libations' from the baraita.
And it is not difficult:
here, it is about libations that come with an animal offering,
phrases.notes: This is the ברייתא that says the מנחה is offered only by day.

phrases.english: there, it is about libations that come by themselves.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא קַשְׁיָא — כָּאן בִּנְסָכִים הַבָּאִין עִם הַזֶּבַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ruling about מנחת נסכים from the earlier discussion, which carries over from before this section.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting cases (אוקימתא): each ברייתא refers to a different kind of נסכים
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two ברייתות contradict each other, so words must be erased from one of them.
steps.terutzMaskana: No words are erased. נסכים brought with a זבח need daytime; נסכים brought alone may be offered at night.

steps.title: Could such a ruling even be sent in a letter?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how a הלכה could be put in a letter at all. רבי יוחנן said that people who write down הלכות are like people who burn the תורה, and someone who learns from them gets no reward.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even if he had a letter, could he really send it? Didn't רבי אבא, son of רבי חייא בר אבא, say in the name of רבי יוחנן: those who write down הלכות are like those who burn the תורה, and whoever learns from them gets no reward?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the plan to send this ruling in writing. It points out that writing down הלכות seems to be forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling in step 1 was meant to be written in a letter. רבי יוחנן's statement suggests that writing down the oral תורה is forbidden, and he describes it very strongly as 'burning the תורה.' So the very idea of sending a written ruling is under attack. Step 5 answers this challenge; first, the גמרא brings more sources about the prohibition.

keyTerms.meaning: A letter
To send it
People who write down הלכות (the oral law)
Like people who burn the תורה
Does not receive reward

steps.confusionAlert: The challenge is not against the ruling about נסכים itself. It only targets the idea of sending that ruling in writing.

phrases.english: And if he had a letter,
would it be possible to send it?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא,
phrases.english: But didn't Rabbi Abba, son of Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba, say
that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
Those who write halakhot are like those who burn the Torah,
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets; the square brackets give the corrected word. Either way, it means 'like those who burn the תורה.'

phrases.english: and one who learns from them does not receive reward.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי הֲוָה לֵיהּ אִיגַּרְתָּא, מִי אֶפְשָׁר לְמִישְׁלְחַהּ? וְהָא אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the method of sending the ruling from step 1, which was to put it in writing.
steps.kashyaTarget: The plan to send the ruling about מנחת נסכים in a letter
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן forbids writing down הלכות and compares it to burning the תורה, so putting a הלכה in a letter should not be allowed.

steps.title: A verse-based teaching against writing the oral words
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה בר נחמני learns from one פסוק that has two phrases. One says 'write' and the other says 'by the mouth.' From this, oral words may not be said from writing, and written words may not be said by heart.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה בר נחמני, the speaker who announced ריש לקיש's lessons, taught: one part of the פסוק says 'Write for yourself these words,' and another part says 'for by the mouth of these words.' This teaches you: words that are oral may not be said in writing, and words that are written may not be said by heart.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a source from the תורה itself that supports the prohibition on writing down the oral teachings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק mentions both writing and 'the mouth.' רבי יהודה בר נחמני reads this as two separate channels. The written תורה stays in writing, and the oral תורה stays oral. This supports רבי יוחנן's statement from step 2, and it also adds the reverse rule: you should not recite written words by heart.

keyTerms.meaning: Expounded; taught a lesson drawn from a פסוק
The speaker who repeated a sage's lesson out loud to the crowd
Words taught orally (the oral תורה)
You are not permitted

steps.whyThisMatters: This is one of the main sources for keeping the תורה שבכתב and the תורה שבעל פה as two separate ways of passing on the תורה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda bar Naḥmani expounded,
the disseminator for Reish Lakish:
phrases.notes: He was the one who said ריש לקיש's words out loud so the whole crowd could hear them.

phrases.english: One verse says:
"Write for yourself these words,"
phrases.notes: שמות 34:27

phrases.english: and one verse says:
"For by the mouth of these words" —
phrases.notes: This is actually the second half of the same פסוק, שמות 34:27.

phrases.english: to tell you:

phrases.aramaic: דְּבָרִים שֶׁעַל פֶּה אִי אַתָּה רַשַּׁאי לְאוֹמְרָן בִּכְתָב,
phrases.english: words that are oral you may not say in writing,

phrases.aramaic: וְשֶׁבִּכְתָב אִי אַתָּה רַשַּׁאי לְאוֹמְרָן עַל פֶּה.
phrases.english: and those that are written you may not say by heart.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּרֵשׁ רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בַּר נַחְמָנִי מְתוּרְגְּמָנֵיהּ דְּרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the prohibition behind the challenge in step 2 with a source from a פסוק.
steps.raayaObject: The prohibition of writing down the oral תורה
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמות 34:27, which mentions both 'write' and 'by the mouth'

steps.title: These you may write, but not הלכות
steps.stepSummary: The school of רבי ישמעאל reads the word 'these' in the פסוק as a limit. Only these words, the written תורה, may be written down. הלכות may not.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the school of רבי ישמעאל taught: 'Write for yourself these words.' These you may write, but you may not write הלכות!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings one more source that backs up the ban on writing down הלכות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the proof comes from a single word, 'these,' which limits the command to write. The words of the written תורה may be written, and nothing else may be. This strengthens the challenge from step 2 against sending a ruling in a letter.

keyTerms.meaning: The school (study house) of רבי ישמעאל
'These,' read as a limit: only these
The rulings of the oral תורה, such as the משניות

steps.whatToRemember: Three sources together, רבי יוחנן, רבי יהודה בר נחמני, and דבי רבי ישמעאל, show that writing down the oral תורה seems forbidden. This sharpens the question of how a ruling could be sent by letter.

phrases.english: And the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
"Write for yourself these words" —
these you may write,
but you may not write halakhot!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתָנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל: ״כְּתׇב לְךָ אֶת הַדְּבָרִים הָאֵלֶּה״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second source, drawn from the word 'these,' for the same prohibition.
steps.raayaObject: The prohibition of writing down הלכות

steps.title: A new teaching may be different
steps.stepSummary: The answer to the question of how the הלכה could be written in a letter: perhaps a new teaching is different and may be written down.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said: Maybe a new teaching is different, and it may be written so it is not forgotten.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 2. How could the הלכה be sent in a letter if writing down הלכות is forbidden?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban on writing down the תורה שבעל פה was just shown from רבי יוחנן's statement and from two readings of one פסוק (שמות 34:27). The answer does not reject that ban. It suggests that a brand-new teaching, which could easily be lost, may be an exception.

keyTerms.meaning: Perhaps, maybe
A new teaching, a new matter
It is different

phrases.english: They said: Perhaps a new matter is different,

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי: דִּלְמָא מִילְּתָא חַדְתָּא שָׁאנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from Step 2, which was backed up by the sources in Steps 3 and 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the rule: the ban on writing has an exception for new teachings.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Writing any הלכה is forbidden, so the letter seems wrong.
steps.terutzMaskana: A new teaching that could be lost may be written down.

steps.title: Reading a book of אגדה, based on 'עת לעשות לה׳'
steps.stepSummary: Proof that writing תורה שבעל פה can be allowed: רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש read from a written book of אגדה. They explained that it is better to set aside one rule than to let the תורה be forgotten.
steps.simpleTranslation: For רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש would read from a book of אגדה on שבת. They explained the פסוק 'It is a time to act for ה׳; they have broken Your תורה' this way: Better that one part of the תורה be uprooted than that the whole תורה be forgotten from ישראל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings support for the idea that writing can be allowed. Great חכמים themselves read from written אגדה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even רבי יוחנן, who called writers of הלכות 'burners of תורה' in Step 2, used a written book. Their reason is the פסוק 'עת לעשות לה׳.' Sometimes one rule must be set aside to save the תורה as a whole. Writing things down keeps the תורה from being forgotten.

keyTerms.meaning: A written book of אגדה (the non-legal teachings of the חכמים)
'It is a time to act for ה׳; they have broken Your Torah,' meaning sometimes a rule is set aside for the sake of ה׳
It is better
Be uprooted

steps.whatToRemember: The ban on writing תורה שבעל פה was set aside so that the תורה would not be forgotten. This is based on 'עת לעשות לה׳ הפרו תורתך.'
steps.confusionAlert: 'Uproot the תורה' does not mean throwing away the תורה. It means setting aside one rule, the ban on writing, to save the whole תורה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This idea explains why we are allowed to have written גמרא and ספרים of תורה שבעל פה today.

phrases.english: For Rabbi Yochanan and Reish Lakish
would read from a book of aggada on Shabbat,
and they expounded like this:
“It is a time to act for the Lord; they have broken Your Torah,”
phrases.notes: תהלים 119:126

phrases.english: They said: It is better that the Torah be uprooted,
phrases.notes: He means uprooting one rule, the ban on writing, not the whole תורה.

phrases.english: and the Torah not be forgotten from Israel.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּהָא רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ מְעַיְּינִי בְּסִיפְרָא דְּאַגַּדְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer in Step 5 by showing that great חכמים used written תורה שבעל פה.
steps.raayaObject: That writing תורה שבעל פה can be allowed when it might otherwise be forgotten.
steps.raayaSupportSource: What רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש did, and their reading of 'עת לעשות לה׳ הפרו תורתך.'

steps.title: נסכים brought by themselves may be made holy and offered at night
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא draws a conclusion from Step 1: if נסכים brought by themselves may be offered at night, they may also be made holy at night and then offered.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Now that you said that נסכים brought by themselves may be offered even at night, if one happens to have נסכים at night, he may make them holy at night and offer them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the main topic of נסכים. רב פפא builds a new rule on top of the answer from Step 1.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 1 said that נסכים brought by themselves, without a זבח, may be offered at night. רב פפא adds that the first stage, making them holy in a כלי שרת, can also happen at night. So the whole process can be done at night.

keyTerms.meaning: נסכים (wine offerings) brought by themselves, not together with a קרבן
They happened to come, they became available
They make them holy (by putting them into a כלי שרת)
They offer them on the מזבח

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: Now that you have said
that libations that come by themselves
are offered even at night,
phrases.notes: This goes back to the answer in Step 1 about נסכים brought without a זבח.

phrases.english: if libations became available at night,
they are consecrated at night and offered.
phrases.notes: Here 'consecrated' means putting the wine into a holy vessel of the בית המקדש.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: הַשְׁתָּא דְּאָמְרַתְּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side topic of writing down הלכות and returns to the rule about נסכים from Step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: נסכים brought by themselves may be made holy at night and offered at night.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רב פפא
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף בריה דרב שמעיה brings a ברייתא with a general rule: whatever may be offered at night may also be made holy at night.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף the son of רב שמעיה said to רב פפא: There is a ברייתא that supports you. 'This is the rule: Anything offered in the day becomes holy only in the day. Anything offered at night becomes holy both in the day and at night.'
steps.whatsHappening: Someone brings a ברייתא to back up what רב פפא just said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא ties the time for making something holy to the time it may be offered. Since נסכים brought by themselves may be offered at night, they may also be made holy at night. That is exactly what רב פפא said.

keyTerms.meaning: That supports you
This is the general rule
Becomes holy (in a כלי שרת)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב יוֹסֵף בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב שְׁמַעְיָה לְרַב פָּפָּא:
phrases.english: Rav Yosef, son of Rav Shemaya, said to Rav Pappa:
It is taught in a baraita in support of you:
“This is the principle: Anything offered in the day
becomes holy only in the day;
and anything offered at night
becomes holy both in the day and at night.”

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא דִּמְסַיַּיע לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב פפא's rule from Step 7.
steps.raayaObject: רב פפא's rule that נסכים brought by themselves may be made holy at night.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: whatever is offered at night becomes holy both by day and by night.

steps.title: Dawn makes these נסכים פסול, like אברים
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה adds a limit: נסכים brought by themselves can be offered at night, but once dawn comes, they become פסול, just like אברים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר אהבה said: And dawn makes them פסול, just like אברים.
steps.whatsHappening: Another אמורא adds a time limit to the night rule. The night lasts only until dawn.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The night allowance is not open-ended. These נסכים follow the same rule as אברים of a קרבן that are burned on the מזבח through the night. Once עלות השחר comes, they become פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: Dawn, when the first light of morning appears
Makes פסול, disqualifies
Limbs of a קרבן that are burned on the מזבח at night

steps.whatToRemember: נסכים brought by themselves may be made holy and offered at night. But at dawn they become פסול, like אברים.

phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Ahava said:
And dawn disqualifies them, like limbs.
phrases.notes: 'Them' means the נסכים brought by themselves. 'Limbs' are the parts of a קרבן burned on the מזבח through the night.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה: וַעֲלוֹת הַשַּׁחַר פּוֹסֶלֶת בָּהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a limit to the night rule from Steps 7 and 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Dawn makes נסכים brought by themselves פסול, as it does for אברים.

steps.title: The first phrase: required festival offerings
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי reports in the name of רבי יוחנן, quoting רבי שמעון בן יהוצדק, that ״אלה תעשו לה׳ במועדיכם״ refers to the offerings that are required on the רגל.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב דימי came from ארץ ישראל, he said that רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי שמעון בן יהוצדק: "These you shall offer to ה׳ in your appointed seasons." These are the required offerings that must be brought on the festival.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new teaching that explains a פסוק about festival offerings. It reads the פסוק one phrase at a time, and this first phrase is about the offerings everyone must bring on the רגל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word ״אלה״ (these) points to a specific group: offerings that are an obligation because of the festival itself. This sets up the rest of the פסוק, which adds other kinds of offerings that may also be brought during the festival.

keyTerms.meaning: In your appointed seasons, meaning the festivals
Required offerings that must be brought
A pilgrimage festival (פסח, שבועות, סוכות)

phrases.english: When Rav Dimi came,
phrases.notes: He came from ארץ ישראל to Bavel and brought teachings from there.

phrases.english: he said that Rabbi Yochanan said
in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Yehotzadak:
"These you shall offer to ה׳ in your appointed seasons"
phrases.notes: במדבר 29:39

phrases.english: these are the required offerings that come
as an obligation on the festival.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתָא רַב דִּימִי, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יְהוֹצָדָק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new teaching that explains the festival-offerings פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ״אלה תעשו לה׳ במועדיכם״ refers to the offerings required because of the רגל.

steps.title: Vowed and voluntary offerings on חול המועד
steps.stepSummary: The phrase ״לבד מנדריכם ונדבותיכם״ teaches that נדרים and נדבות may be offered on חול המועד.
steps.simpleTranslation: "Besides your vows and your voluntary offerings" teaches about vowed and voluntary offerings, that they may be offered on the in-between days of the festival.
steps.whatsHappening: The teaching continues with the next phrase of the פסוק. It says that offerings a person chose to bring may also be offered during חול המועד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word ״לבד״ (besides) adds offerings that are not part of the festival obligation. Even so, they may be brought during the festival days. This gives the basic idea that the rest of the פסוק will build on.

keyTerms.meaning: Vowed offerings, which a person promised to bring
Voluntary offerings, which a person gives freely
The in-between days of the festival (חול המועד)

phrases.english: "Besides your vows and your voluntary offerings"
teaches about vowed and voluntary offerings
that they are offered on the in-between days of the festival.

steps.triggerLanguage: ״לְבַד מִנִּדְרֵיכֶם וְנִדְבוֹתֵיכֶם״ — לִימֵּד עַל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same teaching with the next phrase of the פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: נדרים and נדבות may be offered on חול המועד.

steps.title: Why does the פסוק add 'your burnt offerings'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what ״ולעולותיכם״ adds, since a vowed עולה is already included in ״נדריכם״ and a voluntary עולה is already included in ״נדבותיכם״.
steps.simpleTranslation: "And your burnt offerings": what is the פסוק talking about? If it means a vowed עולה, the פסוק already said "your vows." If it means a voluntary עולה, the פסוק already said "your voluntary offerings."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notices that the word ״עולותיכם״ seems unnecessary. It is setting up the next step, which will explain what this word comes to add.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עולה is either vowed, voluntary, or required. The first two kinds are already covered by the earlier words, so the extra word must be teaching something new.

keyTerms.meaning: What case is the פסוק talking about?
A burnt offering that is burned completely on the מזבח
It was already said, so this word would be extra

phrases.english: "And your burnt offerings"
what is the verse talking about?
If it means a vowed burnt offering
it already said "your vows,"
and if it means a voluntary burnt offering
it already said "your voluntary offerings"!

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּמָה הַכָּתוּב מְדַבֵּר? אִי בְּעוֹלַת נֶדֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks why the פסוק adds a word that seems already covered by Step 11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What kind of עולה the extra word ״ולעולותיכם״ refers to.

steps.title: It means the עולה of a יולדת and of a מצורע
steps.stepSummary: The extra word refers to required עולות of individuals: the עולה of a woman after childbirth and the עולה of a מצורע. These may also be brought on חול המועד.
steps.simpleTranslation: So the פסוק must be talking only about the burnt offering of a woman who gave birth and the burnt offering of a מצורע.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question. ״עולותיכם״ refers to the third kind of עולה, one that a person is required to bring because of what happened to them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These offerings are neither vowed nor voluntary, and they are not festival offerings either. The extra word teaches that they may also be brought during the festival.

keyTerms.meaning: So it must be talking only about
The burnt offering of a woman who gave birth
The burnt offering of a person healed of צרעת

phrases.english: So it is talking only about
the burnt offering of a woman who gave birth and the burnt offering of a metzora.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא אֵינוֹ מְדַבֵּר אֶלָּא בְּעוֹלַת יוֹלֶדֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in Step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ״ולעולותיכם״ refers to the required עולה of a יולדת and of a מצורע.

steps.title: Why does the פסוק add 'your meal offerings'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks the same question about ״ולמנחותיכם״: a vowed מנחה and a voluntary מנחה are already covered.
steps.simpleTranslation: "And your meal offerings": what is the פסוק talking about? If it means a vowed מנחה, that was already said. If it means a voluntary מנחה, that was already said too.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses the same pattern again, this time for meal offerings. It is setting up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reasoning is the same as before. Vowed and voluntary meal offerings are already included in ״נדריכם ונדבותיכם״, so the word ״מנחותיכם״ must be adding a required מנחה.

keyTerms.meaning: A meal offering made from flour
A meal offering that a person vowed to bring

phrases.english: "And your meal offerings"
what is the verse talking about?

phrases.aramaic: אִי בְּמִנְחַת נֶדֶר — הֲרֵי כְּבָר אָמוּר,
phrases.english: If it means a vowed meal offering, it was already said;

phrases.aramaic: אִי בְּמִנְחַת נְדָבָה — הֲרֵי כְּבָר אָמוּר!
phrases.english: if it means a voluntary meal offering, it was already said!

steps.triggerLanguage: ״וּלְמִנְחוֹתֵיכֶם״ — בְּמָה הַכָּתוּב מְדַבֵּר?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks the same kind of question as Step 12, now about meal offerings.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What kind of מנחה the extra word ״ולמנחותיכם״ refers to.

steps.title: It means the מנחה of a סוטה
steps.stepSummary: The extra word refers to the מנחת סוטה, also called the מנחת קנאות. This is a required מנחה that may also be brought on חול המועד.
steps.simpleTranslation: So the פסוק must be talking only about the meal offering of a סוטה, which is the meal offering of jealousy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that ״מנחותיכם״ refers to a required meal offering, the one brought for a סוטה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This matches the answer for עולות. Each extra word adds a required offering of an individual that may also be brought during the festival.

keyTerms.meaning: The meal offering brought for a woman suspected of being unfaithful
The meal offering of jealousy, another name for the מנחת סוטה

steps.confusionAlert: This is not two different offerings. ״מנחת סוטה״ and ״מנחת קנאות״ are two names for the same מנחה.
steps.whatToRemember: The פסוק lists three groups that may be offered at festival time: required festival offerings, נדרים and נדבות, and required offerings of individuals (the עולה of a יולדת or מצורע, and the מנחת סוטה).

phrases.english: So it is talking only about
the meal offering of a sotah, that is, the meal offering of jealousy.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא אֵינוֹ מְדַבֵּר אֶלָּא בְּמִנְחַת סוֹטָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in Step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ״ולמנחותיכם״ refers to the מנחת סוטה, which is the מנחת קנאות.

steps.title: נסכים are compared to שלמים: only by day
steps.stepSummary: The words ״ולנסכיכם ולשלמיכם״ appear next to each other. This compares נסכים to שלמים, so just as שלמים are offered by day, נסכים are also offered by day.
steps.simpleTranslation: ״And your libations and your peace offerings.″ The Torah puts libations next to peace offerings. Just as peace offerings are brought by day, libations are also brought by day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps going through the same פסוק word by word. Now it learns a rule about נסכים from the fact that they are written next to שלמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the פסוק puts the two words side by side, the גמרא treats them as linked, which is called a הֶקֵּשׁ. Whatever is true of שלמים, here that they are offered by day, is true of נסכים too. This is a new kind of lesson: earlier words in the פסוק added more offerings, but this one teaches a rule about when נסכים are offered.

keyTerms.meaning: Libations: wine poured on the מזבח along with certain offerings
Compares, linking two things written next to each other (a הֶקֵּשׁ)
Peace offerings
By day, and not at night

phrases.english: “And your libations and your peace offerings”
phrases.notes: במדבר 29:39, the same פסוק as before.

phrases.english: compares libations to peace offerings:
just as peace offerings are by day,
so too libations are by day.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַקִּישׁ נְסָכִים לִשְׁלָמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the word-by-word reading of the same פסוק that steps 11 to 15 were working through.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: נסכים, like שלמים, may be offered only during the day.

steps.title: The extra word includes the נזיר's peace offering
steps.stepSummary: The word ״ולשלמיכם״ comes to include שלמי נזיר, which may also be brought on חול המועד.
steps.simpleTranslation: ״And your peace offerings″ comes to include the peace offering of a נזיר.
steps.whatsHappening: This follows the same pattern as the steps before it. Voluntary שלמים are already covered by ״נדריכם ונדבותיכם״, so the extra word must be adding a required peace offering: the one a נזיר brings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 13 and 15 used the extra words ״ולעולותיכם״ and ״ולמנחותיכם״ to add required עולות and a required מנחה. Here ״ולשלמיכם״ adds a required שלמים, the שלמי נזיר, which a נזיר brings when his נזירות ends. This is the claim that the next step will challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: To include, adding something the rule would otherwise not cover
The peace offering a נזיר brings when his נזירות ends

phrases.english: “And your peace offerings”
comes to include the peace offering of a nazirite.

steps.triggerLanguage: ״וּלְשַׁלְמֵיכֶם״ — לְרַבּוֹת שַׁלְמֵי נָזִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same pattern as steps 13 and 15: an extra word adds a required offering.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שלמי נזיר may be brought on חול המועד, learned from the extra word ״ולשלמיכם״.

steps.title: אביי suggests the פסח peace offering instead
steps.stepSummary: אביי argues that the extra word should include שלמי פסח, because שלמי נזיר are already a voluntary type of offering and so are already covered.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Let the Master say instead that it includes the peace offering of the פסח. If it means the nazir's peace offering, that offering counts as vowed and freely given.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges step 17. He says the extra word cannot be needed for שלמי נזיר, so it should refer to a different offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The whole method only works if the extra word adds something not already covered by ״נדריכם ונדבותיכם״. אביי claims שלמי נזיר are already in the voluntary group, so the word would be wasted on them. He suggests שלמי פסח, the peace offering brought along with the קרבן פסח, which is a required offering.

keyTerms.meaning: But let the Master say, a polite way to offer a different explanation
The peace offering brought along with the קרבן פסח
Vowed and freely given, meaning a voluntary type of offering

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
phrases.notes: "Him" is the one who taught this reading of the פסוק.

phrases.english: But let the Master say the peace offering of Pesach,
since if it is the nazirite's peace offering,
it is something vowed and freely given.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֵימָא מָר שַׁלְמֵי פֶסַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges which offering the extra word in step 17 really adds.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 17 that ״ולשלמיכם״ comes to include שלמי נזיר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שלמי נזיר are already נידר ונידב, so they are already covered by ״נדריכם ונדבותיכם״. That would make the extra word unnecessary for them, so it should include שלמי פסח instead.

steps.title: First proof: only voluntary offerings go on a private altar
steps.stepSummary: אביי quotes a general rule: any offering that is נידב ונידר may be brought on a בָּמַת יחיד, and any offering that is not may not.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught: This is the rule. Any offering that is freely given or vowed is brought on a private altar. Any offering that is not freely given or vowed is not brought on a private altar.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי begins backing up his claim that שלמי נזיר are voluntary. This first source sets up a test: whatever may go on a private altar must be a voluntary offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This rule links two things: being allowed on a בָּמַת יחיד and being a voluntary offering. On its own it does not mention a נזיר. The next step brings a source that places the נזיר's offerings on the private altar.

keyTerms.meaning: A private altar, which an individual could build in the times it was allowed

phrases.english: As it is taught: This is the rule:
anything that is freely given or vowed
is offered on a private altar,
and whatever is not freely given or vowed
is not offered on a private altar.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּהָתַנְיָא זֶה הַכְּלָל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the support for אביי's claim in step 18.
steps.raayaObject: That שלמי נזיר count as נידר ונידב.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: only offerings that are נידב ונידר are brought on a בָּמַת יחיד.

steps.title: Second proof: נזיר offerings go on a private altar
steps.stepSummary: A second source says that מנחות and the נזיר's offerings are brought on a בָּמַת יחיד, according to רבי מאיר. Put together with the rule in step 19, this means the נזיר's offerings are voluntary.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we learned: Meal offerings and nazirite offerings are brought on a private altar. These are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי finishes his proof. Since the נזיר's offerings may go on a private altar, and only voluntary offerings may go there, the נזיר's offerings must be voluntary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 19 and 20 work together. Step 19 says private altar means voluntary, and step 20 says the נזיר's offerings go on a private altar. So they are voluntary, are already covered by ״נדריכם ונדבותיכם״, and the extra word ״ולשלמיכם״ should not be needed for them.

keyTerms.meaning: Meal offerings
The offerings a נזיר brings

steps.whatToRemember: Two sources combined: private altar means voluntary, and the נזיר's offerings go on a private altar, so they are voluntary.

phrases.english: And we learned: Meal offerings and nazirite offerings
are offered on a private altar,
these are the words of Rabbi Meir!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּתְנַן: הַמְּנָחוֹת וְהַנְּזִירוֹת קְרֵיבִין בְּבָמַת יָחִיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the proof begun in step 19 by placing the נזיר's offerings on the private altar.
steps.raayaObject: That שלמי נזיר are נידר ונידב, so ״ולשלמיכם״ is not needed for them.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A source in the name of רבי מאיר: מנחות and נזירות are brought on a בָּמַת יחיד.

steps.title: Remove the word ״נזירות״ from the source
steps.stepSummary: The answer is to remove ״נזירות״ from the second source. The נזיר's offerings are not counted as voluntary, so ״ולשלמיכם״ is still needed to include them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Remove ״nazirite offerings″ from here.
steps.whatsHappening: The challenge is answered by taking the word ״נזירות״ out of the source quoted in step 20. With that word gone, אביי's proof falls apart.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Taking a נזיר's vow is a free choice, but once he has vowed, his offerings are a requirement. So they are not נידר ונידב and are not already covered. That means the original reading in step 17 stands: ״ולשלמיכם״ includes שלמי נזיר.

keyTerms.meaning: Remove it from here: take a word out of the quoted text

steps.confusionAlert: Becoming a נזיר is voluntary, but the offerings that follow are required. Don't mix up the voluntary vow with the required offerings.
steps.whatToRemember: ״ולשלמיכם״ still includes שלמי נזיר, because the נזיר's offerings are required and not voluntary.

phrases.english: Remove “nazirite offerings” from here.
phrases.notes: "Here" means the source just quoted in step 20.

steps.triggerLanguage: סְמִי מִכָּאן ״נְזִירוֹת״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge by removing the word his proof depended on.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changing the wording of the quoted source by removing a word
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Based on the source in step 20, the נזיר's offerings seem to be voluntary and already covered, so ״ולשלמיכם″ would have to mean שלמי פסח.
steps.terutzMaskana: Take ״נזירות״ out of that source. The נזיר's offerings are required, so ״ולשלמיכם″ is needed to include שלמי נזיר.

steps.title: Is a נזיר's offering really not voluntary? אבשלום went to חברון to pay his vow
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges step 21. It quotes the פסוק about אבשלום paying his vow in חברון, which suggests a נזיר's offering was brought on a private altar.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does anyone really say that a נזיר's offering is not a vowed or voluntary offering? The פסוק says: 'At the end of forty years אבשלום said to the king: Let me go and pay my vow, which I vowed to ה׳, in חברון, for your servant vowed a vow...' Doesn't this mean he went to bring a קרבן there?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from step 21, which took נזירות out of the list of voluntary offerings. It brings a פסוק showing that אבשלום went to חברון to bring his vow offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 21 said a נזיר's offerings are not voluntary, so they cannot go on a בָּמַת יחיד. But אבשלום asked to pay his vow in חברון, away from the main altar, which sounds like a private altar. If he could bring it there, then a נזיר's offering must count as נידר ונידב.

keyTerms.meaning: A person who vowed to avoid wine, haircuts and contact with the dead, and brings offerings at the end
Is it not so that...? (a way of pushing a reading of a source)
An offering brought on the altar

steps.confusionAlert: The פסוק itself does not say the word נזיר. The גמרא understands אבשלום's vow as a vow of נזירות, and that is why it is a challenge here.

phrases.english: Is there anyone who says
that a nazirite is not vowed and donated?
But isn't it written:
"At the end of forty years,
phrases.notes: שמואל ב 15:7–8

phrases.english: Absalom said to the king:
Please let me go and pay my vow
which I vowed to the Lord, in Hebron.
For your servant vowed a vow, etc."
phrases.notes: The rest of the פסוק says he made this vow while living in גשור. That detail comes up in step 24.

phrases.english: Is it not about an offering?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי אִיכָּא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר דְּנָזִיר לָאו נִידָּר וְנִידָּב הוּא? וְהָכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 21, which took נזירות out of the voluntary category
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 21's claim that a נזיר's offerings are not נידר ונידב
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: אבשלום paid his vow with a קרבן in חברון, which means on a private altar. Only voluntary offerings may go on a בָּמַת יחיד (step 19), so a נזיר's offering must be voluntary.

steps.title: No, the vow itself was made in חברון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the words 'in חברון' describe where אבשלום first made his vow, not where he brought the offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. He was talking about the main vow itself, saying that he made it in חברון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends step 21 by reading the פסוק differently. 'In חברון' goes with 'which I vowed', not with 'pay my vow'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If חברון is only where he took on the vow, then the פסוק says nothing about bringing a קרבן there. Without that, there is no proof that a נזיר's offering went on a private altar.

keyTerms.meaning: His main vow itself, the original act of vowing

phrases.english: No, he was speaking about his main vow.
phrases.notes: He means: 'in חברון' tells us where he made the vow, not where he paid it.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, אַעִיקַּר נִדְרוֹ אָמְרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 22
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'In חברון' means he brought his vow offering in חברון
steps.terutzMaskana: 'In חברון' means he made his original vow in חברון, so no offering is described there

steps.title: But the vow was made in גשור, not חברון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: the same פסוק says אבשלום made his vow while living in גשור, so it could not have been made in חברון.
steps.simpleTranslation: Was his main vow made in חברון? It was made in גשור!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the answer of step 23. The פסוק itself says the vow was made in גשור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The next פסוק says, 'your servant vowed a vow while I lived in גשור in ארם.' So 'in חברון' cannot be the place of the vow. The challenge from step 22 comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: A kingdom in ארם where אבשלום lived after running away from דוד
But isn't it so...! (introduces a clear fact that contradicts what was just said)

phrases.english: Was his main vow in Hebron?
But it was in Geshur!
phrases.notes: This comes from the next פסוק, שמואל ב 15:8, where he says he vowed while living in גשור.

steps.triggerLanguage: עִיקַּר נִדְרוֹ בְּחֶבְרוֹן הֲוָה? וַהֲלֹא בִּגְשׁוּר הֲוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer of step 23
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that 'in חברון' is where the vow was made
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק itself says the vow was made in גשור, so חברון cannot be the place of the vow.

steps.title: אבשלום only went to חברון to bring sheep
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא, or some say רבה בר רב חנן, answers that אבשלום went to חברון only to get sheep for his offering, not to offer them there.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא said, and some say it was רבה בר רב חנן: אבשלום only went to bring sheep from חברון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new answer to the challenge of step 22. אבשלום's trip to חברון was to get animals, not to bring them on an altar there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the trip was only to get sheep, he could still bring the offering at the proper altar. Then the פסוק does not show that a נזיר's offering went on a בָּמַת יחיד, and step 21 stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Sheep (lambs), the animals a נזיר brings as offerings

phrases.english: Rav Aḥa said,
and some say it was Rabba bar Rav Ḥanan:
Absalom went only
to bring sheep from Hebron.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא הָלַךְ אַבְשָׁלוֹם אֶלָּא לְהָבִיא כְּבָשִׂים מֵחֶבְרוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a new answer after step 24 knocked down the first one
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the purpose of the trip
steps.terutzHavaAmina: He went to חברון to offer the קרבן there on a private altar
steps.terutzMaskana: He went to חברון only to get sheep, so no private altar is described

steps.title: Support: he would not leave ירושלים to offer in חברון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports the sheep answer: it makes sense, because nobody would leave ירושלים to bring an offering in חברון.
steps.simpleTranslation: This also makes sense. If you say he went to offer the קרבן, would he leave ירושלים and go offer it in חברון?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up the answer of step 25 with simple reasoning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ירושלים was the main place for offerings, so it would be strange to leave it and offer somewhere else. That makes the reading 'he went just to get sheep' more likely.

keyTerms.meaning: This also makes sense (logic that supports the answer just given)
Leaves, abandons

phrases.english: This also makes sense,
for if you say
that he went to offer a sacrifice —
would he leave Jerusalem
and go and offer in Hebron?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי נָמֵי מִסְתַּבְּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of step 25
steps.raayaObject: That אבשלום went to חברון only to get sheep
steps.raayaSupportSource: Logic: no one would leave ירושלים, the main place for offerings, to offer in חברון

steps.title: Then the פסוק should say 'from חברון', not 'in חברון'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the sheep answer: if he was only getting sheep from חברון, the פסוק should say 'from חברון', not 'in חברון'.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what are you saying, that he went to bring sheep from חברון? Then the words 'which I vowed to ה׳ in חברון' should have said 'from חברון'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer of step 25 using the exact wording of the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says בְּחֶבְרוֹן, 'in חברון', which sounds like something happened there. If the point was only to get sheep, it should say מֵחֶבְרוֹן, 'from חברון'. So the sheep answer does not fit the words.

keyTerms.meaning: But then what? (questions an answer by spelling out what it would mean)
It should have said (the wording should have been different)

steps.whyThisMatters: Both readings that would protect step 21 have now run into trouble. Steps 28 and 29 go back to the plain reading, that אבשלום went to חברון to bring his offering.

phrases.english: But rather, what?
To bring sheep from Hebron?
Then this "which I vowed to the Lord, in Hebron",
should have said "from Hebron"!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֶלָּא מַאי? לְהָבִיא כְּבָשִׂים מֵחֶבְרוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 25 even after the support in step 26
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that אבשלום only went to get sheep from חברון
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק says 'in חברון' (בְּחֶבְרוֹן), not 'from חברון' (מֵחֶבְרוֹן), so it does not fit a trip just to get sheep.

steps.title: Back to the plain reading: he went to bring the offering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops the sheep answer and says אבשלום really went to חברון to sacrifice. It then shows that the question 'why leave ירושלים?' is not a real question, since by that logic you would have to ask why he did not go to גבעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he really went to חברון to sacrifice. As for your question, 'Why would he leave ירושלים and sacrifice in חברון?': you should really be asking about גבעון, because that was a holy place!
steps.whatsHappening: Since 'in חברון' does not fit the sheep answer, the גמרא returns to the simple meaning: he went there to bring his offering. It then takes apart the reasoning from step 26.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 26 assumed nobody would leave ירושלים to sacrifice in חברון. The גמרא answers that ירושלים was not the special place at that time, because the משכן was in גבעון. So the real question would be why he skipped גבעון. That question sets up the answer in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Actually, really (used when returning to the original or plain explanation)
To sacrifice, to bring an offering
The city where the משכן and main מזבח stood at that time
A holy place

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think ירושלים was the holy place of offerings in אבשלום's time. The בית המקדש had not been built yet, and the משכן was in גבעון.

phrases.english: Rather, actually [he went] to sacrifice,
and as for what is difficult for you:
why did he leave Jerusalem
and sacrifice in Hebron?
let Gibeon be difficult for you,
phrases.notes: In other words: if you want to ask a question, ask why he didn't go to גבעון.

phrases.english: for it is a holy place!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לְעוֹלָם לְאַקְרוֹבֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the challenge of step 27, abandons the sheep answer, and undoes the reasoning of step 26.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Return to the plain reading, with the opposing question turned around
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Going to חברון to sacrifice makes no sense when ירושלים is nearby, so he must have gone only for sheep.
steps.terutzMaskana: He did go to sacrifice. Leaving ירושלים is not the issue; the only possible question is why he skipped גבעון.

steps.title: Private altars were permitted, so he could offer anywhere
steps.stepSummary: Since במות (private altars) were permitted at that time, a person could bring his offering wherever he wanted, so choosing חברון needs no special reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, since private altars were permitted, a person could sacrifice wherever he wanted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own גבעון question. במות were allowed then, so אבשלום could sacrifice in חברון or anywhere else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a time when במות are permitted, no single place is required for this kind of offering. So there is no question about leaving ירושלים, and none about skipping גבעון. The plain reading, 'he went to sacrifice in חברון', stands. That means the answers to the challenge in step 22 have fallen away: the פסוק does describe אבשלום bringing his vow offering on a private altar.

keyTerms.meaning: Private altars, which were permitted to be used during certain periods
Were permitted
Wherever he wants

steps.whatToRemember: אבשלום really did go to חברון to bring his offering. This was allowed because במות were permitted, so any place was acceptable. That means his נזיר offering went on a private altar, which fits the challenge in step 22 rather than step 21's removal of ״נזירות״.

phrases.english: Rather, since private altars were permitted
wherever he wants, he sacrifices.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, כֵּיוָן שֶׁהוּתְּרוּ הַבָּמוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the גבעון question raised in step 28 and closes the discussion about חברון.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Because במות were permitted, אבשלום could sacrifice anywhere, so offering in חברון is fully explained. The reading behind the challenge in step 22, that he brought his vow offering on a private altar, stands.

steps.title: Forty years counted from when?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what starting point the 'forty years' in the פסוק about אבשלום are counted from.
steps.simpleTranslation: Forty years: counted from what?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new detail in the same פסוק. It asks where the 'forty years' begin, and the answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'at the end of forty years' without saying what the count starts from. The גמרא needs to find the starting point of the count.

keyTerms.meaning: For whom? Here: counted from what point?
Forty years

phrases.english: Forty years, from whose [counting]?
phrases.notes: שמואל ב 15:7

steps.triggerLanguage: אַרְבָּעִים שָׁנָה, לְמַאן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new question about the same פסוק, now that the חברון issue is settled.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The starting point of the 'forty years' mentioned in the פסוק.

steps.title: From when the people asked for a king
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי נהוראי in the name of רבי יהושע: the forty years are counted from when בני ישראל asked for a king.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: רבי נהוראי says in the name of רבי יהושע: 'At the end of forty years' means forty years from when they asked for a king.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question with a ברייתא. The count starts from the time the people asked שמואל for a king.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The starting point is not the beginning of דוד's reign. It is the earlier event when the nation first requested a king. This explains how the number reaches forty.

keyTerms.meaning: At the end of
When they asked for a king for themselves

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Nehorai says
in the name of Rabbi Yehoshua:
"At the end of forty years"
from when they asked for themselves a king,

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא: רַבִּי נְהוֹרַאי אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 30.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The forty years are counted from when בני ישראל asked for a king.

steps.title: That year was שמואל's tenth year
steps.stepSummary: A second ברייתא supports the timeline: the year the people asked for a king was the tenth year of שמואל's leadership.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught in a ברייתא: the year they asked for a king was the tenth year of שמואל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another ברייתא to pin down when the people asked for a king. It was in שמואל's tenth year as leader.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This fixes the starting point of the count on a known timeline. Counting from שמואל's tenth year, the forty years can be lined up with the years of שמואל, שאול and דוד.

keyTerms.meaning: Tenth
That same year

phrases.english: As it was taught: that year
when they asked for themselves a king,
that year was the tenth
of Samuel.
phrases.notes: He means the tenth year of שמואל leading the people.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: אוֹתָהּ שָׁנָה שֶׁשָּׁאֲלוּ לָהֶם מֶלֶךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 31 by placing the request for a king on a known timeline.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that the forty years start from the request for a king.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא stating that the request for a king happened in שמואל's tenth year.
